newsitem.title: USA: Harley Q3 up on motorcycle, parts sales.
newsitem.headline: Harley Q3 up on motorcycle, parts sales.

text.p: Harley-Davidson Inc said on Tuesday that improved third-quarter results came on an increase in motorcycle unit shipments and improved performance in the company's parts and accessories business.
Third quarter unit shipments totaled 28,013 units, up 12 percent from a year ago. Parts and Accessories sales totaled $90.5 million, up 19.3 percent over a year earlier.

"We're on track with our production capacity expansion efforts and are scheduled to ship 118,000 units in 1996 (up 12.3 percent from 105,100 units in 1995)," said chairman and chief executive Richard Teerlink.

"Our new model year change-over was the smoothest in recent memory and our production facilities averaged 490 units per day, with very minimal assembly line overtime. We have increased our motorcycle production rate and are scheduled to average 510 units per day in the fourth quarter," he said.
Motorcycle production exceeded motorcycle shipments by approximately 900 units in the third quarter, Harley said.

"This was primarily the result of an inventory build-up at our wholly owned French and German distributors," Teerlink said. "Demand for heavyweight motorcycles ... is strong in Europe, but Harley-Davidson is experiencing mixed results."

Year-to-date shipments in most of Europe were up over last year, but shipments to Germany and France were down, resulting in a 6.9 percent year-over-year rise in European shipments, Harley said. Teerlink said he doesn't expect to see the full impact of certain new initiatives in Europe until next year.

The company on Tuesday reported third-quarter sales of $385.8 million, up 18 percent from the year-ago quarter. Net income and earnings per share were $33.2 million, or $0.44 per share, versus $23.7 million, or $0.32 a year ago. Prior-year figures were restated to reflect the company's transportation vehicles segment as a discontinued operation.

Data through July show that in the U.S. market for heavy motorcycles of 751cc's and up, Harley-Davidson held a 51.7 percent market share, compared with 52.6 percent in the year-ago period. The U.S. heavy-motorcycle market grew at a 15.3 percent rate year-to-date, Harley said.

European data through July show Harley holding a 9.2 percent share of the 751+cc market, down from 10.5 last year. The European 751+cc market grew at a 13.3 percent rate year-to-date, while retail registrations for Harley-Davidson motorcycles were about the same as last year, the company said.

"The demand for Harley-Davidson motorcycles in the U.S. continues to exceed the supply allocated to our U.S. dealers," Teerlink said. Due to conditions in Europe, he said, the U.S. allocation of 1997 model year motorcycles was raised to 72 percent of total output, up from 70 percent in previous years.

Third quarter parts and accessories sales totaled $90.5 million, up 19.3 percent from a year ago. Parts sales were up 20.4 percent a year ago; clothing and collectibles were up 17.1 percent. "It is important to remember, however, that last year's third quarter P&A results were below our expectations," Teerlink said.
He added, "Although 1996 total year P&A sales will not meet our expectations, we still expect long-term P&A revenue growth to approximate the company's growth rate in motorcycle unit shipments."
Harley's financial services segment reported third quarter operating income of $1.3 million versus $800,000 in the year-ago quarter.
